title: Sable Capital private deploy & gated-data call notes
content:
Call 2025-11-07 — 10:00 PST (initial technical scoping)
Participants: Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood Solutions), Leah (Redwood PM), Omar (Sable infra lead), Claire (Sable security/compliance), Ben (Sable data engineering)

High-level ask
- Sable Capital wants an on-prem / VPC-hosted inference deployment to run LLM features over gated customer financial data.
- Primary features: document Q&A (RAG), embeddings for similarity search across 30M documents, and secure extraction pipeline for KYC fields.
- Must meet strict data residency & audited key management requirements.

Constraints noted by customer
- Data cannot leave their VPC. No outbound egress to third-party hosted endpoints.
- KMS must be FIPS 140-2 (or 140-3) compatible and integrate with their HSM fleet (Thales HSM).
- Audit trail retention: minimum 3 years for access logs; prefer 7 years for some regulated assets (confirm exact bucket).
- Low-latency SLO for interactive Q&A: p95 <= 450ms for 512-token responses; concurrently supporting 10–12 agents.
- Batch embedding throughput target: ~50k embeddings/day to start; burst up to 300k/day during reindex windows.
- Approved cloud region: AWS us-east-2 primary; potential on-prem racks in their NY data center for cold workloads.

Environmental details (from Ben)
- Typical doc size: avg 2.5KB, 95th percentile ~80KB. Many PDFs scanned with OCR noise.
- Upstream vector store is a managed PostgreSQL + pgvector today; they are open to Milvus/FAISS for scaling but need guidance.
- PII scrub required pre-ingest. They want Redwood to help validate tokenization + PII redaction step as part of PoC.

Redwood product fit possibilities discussed
- Redwood Private (VPC) with customer-managed control plane appears to map well to their egress + KMS requirements.
- Dedicated/reserved GPUs on their VPC vs on-prem racks: tradeoffs discussed — on-prem gives full physical control for HSM but adds ops.
- Suggestion: start with VPC Private deployment using customer VPC peering + AWS KMS (FIPS), with a later option to swap to on-prem package if audits require.

Technical gotchas / risks called out (capture here so solutions team can craft mitigations)
- KV-cache warmup: interactive latency targets will be hard until prompt/seq-length distributions stabilize. Need warmed prefixes or dynamic warming plan.
- OCR/noisy PDFs will inflate token counts -> cost/latency. Recommend sampling + custom text-cleaning; maybe early stop threshold for OCR garbage pages.
- HSM integration: Redwood Private currently supports KMS integrations; direct Thales HSM plug-in will need SRE/infra time (estimated 2–3 sprints).
- Network topology: requirement for private control plane inside their VPC might conflict with our telemetry/tracing hooks. Need explicit whitelist/collector design (customers are strict about no telemetry leaving).
- Embedding drift: they want regression alerts. Need baseline eval set + cadence for re-eval; Redwood Optimize can help but will need seed prompt set from Sable.

Questions we must answer (actionable)
- Claire: "Do you support FIPS-validated KMS with customer-owned HSMs?" (Action: confirm exact HSM model + required operators).
- Ben: "What does token billing look like if we do heavy OCR processing?" (Action: provide example cost breakdown for 1M token/day with additional OCR overhead).
- Omar: "Can control plane run entirely in our VPC with no external egress?" (Action: ops runbook for fully air-gapped deployment; note: extra license + engineering work).
- SLA: they asked for formal 99.9% uptime for private deployments — need to confirm enterprise SLA options & escalation matrix.

Immediate PoC plan (proposed)
1) PoC scope (2–4 weeks):
   - Deploy Redwood Private in Sable's us-east-2 VPC (single AZ) with test GPUs; integrate AWS KMS FIPS option.
   - Ingest a 100k-document sample (subset Ben will supply) through our ingestion pipeline with pre-ingest PII scrub heuristics enabled.
   - Implement embedding pipeline to their pgvector test instance and run latency/throughput benchmarks.
   - Run 1000 interactive Q&A sessions (simulated agents) to collect p50/p95 latency and failure modes.
2) Deliverables:
   - Architecture diagram + network config for approval.
   - Performance report (latency, tokens, cost estimates) and a gap/security checklist.
   - Proposal for next milestone (dedicated capacity vs on-prem license).
3) Timeline: Kickoff this week if approvals come through; aim for staging PoC environment in 7 business days.

Owners / who does what
- Redwood: Priya (technical lead / PoC run), Marco (ops + infra liaison), Leah (PM / deliverables), Eng-SRE on-call for network config (TBD).
- Sable: Omar (infra lead), Ben (data engineering), Claire (security/compliance), Legal contact TBD (for contract addendum).

Budget / procurement flags
- They asked for an order-of-magnitude cost for a 4-week PoC (~Dedicated + SRE time). I gave a high-level estimate verbally (~$15–25k) — need to formalize.
- Procurement: Sable will likely require a short MSA + addendum for data residency and audit support. Legal to loop in after PoC scope finalized.

Notes to self (SE playbook items)
- Prepare a small doc: "Redwood Private — air-gapped checklist" (include control plane footprint, required ports, telemetry opt-out).
- Create sample cost model spreadsheet: inputs = doc count, avg tokens/doc, OCR multiplier, QPS, batch size -> tokens/day -> cost.
- Reuse Optimize suggestions: default quantization recommendation for their workload is int8-based (but verify accuracy on financial text).

Next steps (short list)
- [Priya] Draft architecture diag + PoC runbook and share with Omar by 2025-11-10.
- [Marco] Confirm KMS/HSM integration feasibility with infra team (ENG-7123) and estimate effort by 2025-11-12.
- [Leah] Put together formal PoC quote & SOW skeleton; include estimated SRE hours. Target 2025-11-12.
- [Ben/Omar] Provide 100k doc sample + example pgvector schema by 2025-11-09.
- [Claire] Send compliance checklist items (minimum KMS certs, audit frequencies) by 2025-11-11.

Loose thoughts / brainstorming (freeform)
- Could offer a hybrid: embeddings in their VPC, but less-sensitive quick inference on Redwood Dedicated as a cache-enabled fallback — gives cost flexibility while preserving most sensitive flows inside VPC. Need to validate legal on fallbacks (Claire probably no).
- For OCR docs, a quick wins: run a 2-pass pipeline (lightweight fast-clean then full OCR) and surface confidence scores to drop low-value pages early.

Open/parking-lot items
- Legal: contract addendum for data residency & indemnities (owner: Leah).
- Security: pen-test schedule if they want annual attestation.
- Long-term: roadmap conversation about supporting fully air-gapped control plane (time + price).

End notes
- Call ended with Sable enthusiastic but cautious. Main gating items: KMS/HSM fit, SLA, and a clean PoC sample dataset.
- Overall signal: high intent if PoC shows acceptable latency/cost.

-- Priya
(quick capture; will iterate after Marco & Leah updates)
